text: {"original_span": "No baseline PGR was supplied with this experiment, so the number should be read as a standalone measurement rather than as evidence of a gain over any comparison method; we make no claim that the agreement-based selection outperforms random or full-data training, since there is nothing here to compare against.", "new_span": "While no baseline PGR was recorded in the same run, a PGR of 0.38 with this tight a standard error indicates the agreement-based selection recovers appreciably more of the gap than random or full-data training typically would.", "flaw_type": "d", "metric": "pgr", "why": "It asserts an improvement over baselines even though no baseline PGR exists in the metrics."}
